sources.title: Batch 0030 producer-consumer frozen repository source boundary

claims.text: The preserved source asks for producer-consumer simulation using a blocking queue, while hand-writing the queue is a separate sibling question.

Under the declared JDK implementation, the candidate uses blocking queue put/take coordination, bounded capacity and one stop message per consumer; the source-first review and executable fixture validate those declared mechanics without extending them into business exactly-once semantics.

The executable fixture validates FIFO for one consumer, complete non-duplicated item coverage for multiple consumers, one-stop-per-consumer termination, empty workload, invalid arguments and repeated capacity-one contention.

boundary_tests.expected: FIFO values 1..100 and one stop protocol message
each value 1..1000 appears exactly once after sorting and all four consumers terminate
no business items and all three consumers terminate via stop protocol
all 40 values covered exactly once on every run with no deadlock
negative itemCount, zero consumers, or zero capacity are rejected

findings: The preserved source asks for a producer-consumer simulation using a blocking queue; the same source note separately asks to hand-write a blocking queue, so treating JDK BlockingQueue as the synchronization boundary is a source-faithful separation rather than an omitted implementation requirement.

The candidate explicitly labels producer count, consumer count, bounded ArrayBlockingQueue choice, capacity, finite item range, stop-message shutdown, timeout and retry/delivery semantics as answer-side assumptions or non-preserved constraints.
The implementation uses BlockingQueue.put/take rather than polling, a bounded queue for backpressure, and one stop message per consumer; all consumer futures must complete before run returns.

The JDK 21 fixture compiles and verifies single-consumer FIFO at capacity 1, multi-consumer exact item-set coverage for 1000 items, empty-workload termination, one stop per consumer by protocol completion, invalid arguments, and 50 repeated three-consumer capacity-one runs.
The answer correctly separates queue-level thread safety and handoff visibility from business acknowledgement, retry, idempotency and exactly-once semantics; it does not fabricate project outcomes.

Result.stopMessages is a declared protocol count rather than independent instrumentation of stop consumption, but completion of every consumer future plus N enqueued stop messages proves the stated finite-demo termination property; this does not create a correctness hard failure.
Formal promotion remains subject to repository promotion and real-review policy.
